parity_notes: No product source changed anywhere; frozen surfaces untouched (RPC exercised as a black box over stdio). The TS anchor fixes the reference semantics for this class: (a) one IpythonKernelProvisioner (one kernel process) per AgentSession — a replacement generation is a fresh session and spawns a second kernel, same shape as Rust (agent-session.ts:1691, :10810-10828); (b) the new_session/switch_session/fork response wall awaits the OLD session's teardown (old kernel snapshot flush + drain + graceful shutdown, 5s-capped) but NEVER the new kernel's boot — the replacement session's prewarm is fire-and-forget (rpc-mode.ts:480, agent-session-runtime.ts:474-496, agent-session.ts:10906-10908, ipython.ts:385-388); (c) cold venv: concurrent boots join the in-flight ensureKernelPython promise or contend on the on-disk bootstrap lock with a post-acquire re-check — one materialization, each kernel still its own process (bootstrap.ts:1027-1036, :999-1003); (d) TS aborts a mid-boot kernel on dispose (raceStartupWithAbort repl-manager.ts:341; not-yet-running skips the snapshot flush). Rust matches (a)(b)(c) — measured here: fresh kernel generation per replacement, background boot, walls carrying only old-kernel teardown, walls flat across sequential replacements. ONE divergence on (d), documented in-tree as intentional (provisioner.rs:510-525 raced_dispose) — see measurements.zombie_boot_on_raced_dispose. NO CANDIDATE taken, per the brief's trivial-TS-parity bar: the zombie-boot fix (racing an abort into do_start) touches the kernel start/teardown seam = armed-lane measurement-only territory; the in-tree comment frames the current behavior as deliberate; there is no wall/regression to win (all cost is background). EOF exit parity is true (main.rs:9 exits without awaiting background boots; TS runRpcMode returns at EOF with the ensure un-awaited) — liveness finding only.

decision: The cold second-kernel-boot class is CLOSED at tip a5235b123: no RPC replacement flavor (new_session/switch_session/fork), warm or cold-venv, steady-state or mid-materialization, ever pays kernel boot or venv materialization on its response wall — max 142ms across 17 trials (the 10MiB fork parse class); the source 10.8s observation is attributed to the pre-fix rpc-baseline driver (its own record flagged it not-clean) and is not a product class. The replacement wall is old-kernel teardown + build + rebind; the second kernel is per-generation, boots in the background (67-119ms execve->ready, venv one-shot 0.6-0.9s warm-cache, probe memoized per venv) and joins on the first ipython call — exactly the TS contract (anchor Q2/Q6). Two findings are left for the kernel-surface owner, both documented and neither a wall regression: (1) the raced_dispose zombie boot (Rust completes a mid-boot boot then tears it down; TS aborts — provisioner.rs:510-525, background-only cost, worst case one wasted boot + sub-200ms next-session kernel-readiness delay); (2) EOF exit never awaits in-flight venv materialization (parity-true liveness note; a partial venv re-materializes on next boot). No candidate meets the #2953 trivial-TS-parity bar: the zombie-boot fix is a real cancellation change on armed-lane territory with zero wall benefit.
